target.title: feat(android): add Skill Workshop settings panel
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android Settings did not expose the Skill Workshop review queue, so mobile users could not inspect generated skill proposals or perform the same core proposal lifecycle actions available from the Web UI. This left proposal review dependent on desktop/Web access even when the Android app was already connected to a Gateway.

## Summary

- Add a dedicated Android Settings > Skill Workshop panel for proposal review.
- Load proposal lists and details through existing Gateway `skills.proposals.*` RPCs with agent-scope support.
- Auto-load selected proposal details to match Web controller behavior.
- Support pending proposal lifecycle actions from mobile: apply, reject, and quarantine.
- Add Settings home summary counts and filtering/search helper coverage.

## Implementation Notes

- The Android UI uses a mobile list/detail layout rather than the Web desktop board layout.
- No new Gateway API is introduced; Android reuses the existing Skill Workshop RPC methods.
- Gateway responses are guarded against stale list/detail updates during gateway changes.

## Evidence

- Local static checks passed on the PR branch:
  - `git diff --check`
  - `git diff --cached --check`
- Added unit coverage for Skill Workshop settings summary and filtering helpers in `ShellScreenLogicTest`.
- GitHub Actions on this PR has reported passing checks for Workflow Sanity `no-tabs`, `actionlint`, OpenGrep PR diff, dependency guard, security-sensitive guard, Socket PR alerts, CI `runner-admission`, `preflight`, and `security-fast`.
- Android-specific CI checks are running on GitHub Actions for this branch, including `android-ktlint`, `android-build-play`, `android-test-play`, and `android-test-third-party`.

## Not Run Locally

- Android ktlint/build/tests were not run locally because this environment has no `java`/`JAVA_HOME` available. The Android verification matrix is running in GitHub Actions.

## Risk

- Moderate UI/RPC surface change isolated to Android Settings and existing Skill Workshop Gateway methods.
- No dependency, workflow, release, or Gateway API surface changes.
